intent: Can I put artificial turf on a Parker property, and which Town code section, office and water district decide?
distinctValue: Parker is the one page that carries the Town's own synthetic-turf rule. Parker Municipal Code 13.08.090 (Supplement 26.1, codified through Ordinance No. 4.119, passed March 23, 2026) prohibits synthetic turf within landscaped areas, with three Town-approved exceptions: school and Town athletic or recreation facilities, private outdoor recreational facilities, and pet relief areas for vet clinics, kennels and dog parks. Table 13.08.L sets no site-landscaping or living-coverage minimum for single-family detached lots, and Table 13.08.M marks only streetscape landscaping for them, so a detached back yard is a different question from a commercial, multifamily or pet-business site; the page asks Planning to confirm rather than asserting either way. Also local and not on any neighbour page: 13.08.130 keeps approved landscape plans in force 'in perpetuity, unless amended or modified by the Town', the LDO Administrative Manual (May 2024) requires every landscape plan to note that changes need Town and Water and Sanitation District approval, kennels and pet grooming shops must provide pet relief areas (13.05.030), and the Town's park design criteria call for living or synthetic turf in open play areas with artificial turf preferred for ball fields. PWSD's three-day schedule, its multifamily/HOA/commercial day, the new-sod permit and the $750 Resource Central discount (turf eligibility not stated) are re-verified. Lone Tree's page carries PWSD days for its east side only; the wording here is new.

(b) Applicability. (1) New, non-infill development shall comply fully with the standards in this Section 13.08.090.

a. Minor Improvements. Any changes to a property or use that do not add building square footage, such as architectural changes or changes to comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act, shall not be required to install additional landscaping.

b. Moderate Improvements. Square footage changes that increase the total gross floor area of a structure by less than seventy-five (75) percent, or that add new parking areas, storage, or that expand the use, as determined by the Building Permit and Site Plan applications, shall include a corresponding percent increase in compliance with this Section 13.08.090, as determined by the Planning Director.

c. Large Improvements. Square footage changes that increase total gross floor area of a structure by seventy-five (75) percent or greater ... shall be required to fully comply with this Section 13.08.090.

(3) All developments requiring Site Plan approval and/or streetscape landscaping shall submit a landscaping plan meeting all applicable requirements on the Town website, in order to enable the Town to evaluate compliance with this Section 13.08.090.

Table 13.08.L: Total Landscaping Requirements. Min. Site Landscaping (% of Developed Area): Single-Family Detached/Duplex n/a; Single-Family Attached 35%; Multifamily 45%; Mixed-Use 25%; Nonresidential 15%; Downtown (DE, DW) 10%.
Min. Living Material Coverage (% of Developed Area): Single-Family Detached/Duplex n/a; Single-Family Attached 75%; Multifamily 75%; Mixed-Use 75%; Nonresidential 75%; Downtown 75%.

Table 13.08.M: Landscaping and Buffering Applicability. Streetscape 13.08.090 (e): checked for Single-Family Detached/Duplex and every other column. Parking Lot Interior, Site Perimeter and Site Interior: n/a for Single-Family Detached/Duplex.
(2) Applicability. Streetscape landscaping is required for all development in all zoning districts.

a. Streetscape landscaping that complies with this Section 13.08.090 (e) shall be installed in the area between each curb and a detached sidewalk, or in the case of an attached sidewalk, within eight (8) feet from the back of the sidewalk away from the street.
d. All property owners including residential property owners shall be responsible for maintaining, repairing, and replacing streetscape landscaping, including street trees and ground cover
(4) Specific requirements. Streetscape landscaping shall consist of trees and turf grass or shrubs, rock, and mulch that meet the following standards.

c. Non-living landscape material standards. 1. Artificial landscape materials, including, for example, plastic trees, shrubs, and synthetic turf, are prohibited within landscaped areas. Exceptions to this prohibition include the following, as approved by the Town:
a) Athletic or recreation facilities at public or private schools and Town-owned property or parks; and
b) Private outdoor recreational facilities.
c) Synthetic turf and similar materials may be considered for specific purposes for land uses such as pet relief areas for veterinary clinics, kennels, or dog parks.
2. Non-living landscape areas shall not count towards the minimum landscape requirements.

sources.label: Parker Municipal Code §13.08.130, Maintenance and operating standards (same API retrieval, job 493493)
supports: All properties in the Town shall comply with the standards in this Section 13.08.130 regarding the operation and maintenance of activities, buildings, and land in the Town.

b. The trees, shrubs, fences, walls, and other landscaping materials depicted on approved plans shall be considered as elements of the project in the same manner as parking, building materials and other elements, and shall be maintained in perpetuity, unless amended or modified by the Town.

d. For all required landscaping and planting, dead plant materials shall be removed and replaced with healthy planting materials of comparable size and species that meet the original intent of the approved landscape design within forty-five (45) days after the plant dies, or if seasonal conditions prohibit removal and replacement then by June 1.
